title: The Tower of Babel
excerpt: The whole earth shares “one language and a common form of speech” (v 1). Migrating eastward, the people settle on the plain of Shinar. They devise a new technology—“bricks for stone and bitumen for mortar” (v 3)—and resolve, “Come, let us build ourselves a city, with a tower whose top reaches to the heavens. Let us make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered over the face of all the earth” (v 4). Their project unites them in pride and resistance against God’s earlier command to fill the earth. The LORD “came down to see the city and the tower” (v 5). He notes that one language and purpose empower limitless rebellion (v 6). In judgment and mercy He confuses their language, halting construction. The place is called Babel, “because there the LORD confused the language of the whole earth” (v 9). He scatters the people “over the face of the whole earth,” accomplishing His original design. A genealogy traces ten generations from Shem to Abram: Shem–Arphaxad–Shelah–Eber–Peleg–Reu–Serug–Nahor–Terah–Abram. Lifespans shorten again, yet the promise-bearing line remains intact. Terah fathers Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran dies early, leaving his son Lot. Abram marries Sarai, who is barren. Terah sets out from Ur of the Chaldeans toward Canaan, taking Abram, Sarai, and Lot, but settles in Harran, where he dies.This chapter introduces a significant moment in human history, where humanity, speaking one language, builds a tower to reach the heavens in defiance of God's command. Their unity leads to God's intervention, scattering them across the earth and confounding their language. The chapter then traces the lineage from Shem to Abram, who embarks on a journey to the land of Canaan but settles in Haran.

people.name: Shem
people.description: The son of Noah, from whom the Semitic peoples are descended. Shem is significant as the ancestor of Abram (later Abraham).

people.name: Arphaxad
people.description: The son of Shem, born two years after the flood. His name in Hebrew is אַרְפַּכְשַׁד (Arpakhshad).

people.name: Shelah
people.description: The son of Arphaxad. His name in Hebrew is שֶׁלַח (Shelach).

people.name: Eber
people.description: The son of Shelah, from whom the term "Hebrew" is derived. His name in Hebrew is עֵבֶר (Eber).

people.name: Peleg
people.description: The son of Eber, during whose days the earth was divided. His name in Hebrew is פֶּלֶג (Peleg).

people.name: Reu
people.description: The son of Peleg. His name in Hebrew is רְעוּ (Re'u).

people.name: Serug
people.description: The son of Reu. His name in Hebrew is שְׂרוּג (Serug).

people.name: Nahor
people.description: The son of Serug. His name in Hebrew is נָחוֹר (Nachor).

people.name: Terah
people.description: The son of Nahor, and the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. His name in Hebrew is תֶּרַח (Terach).

people.name: Abram
people.description: The son of Terah, later known as Abraham, a key patriarch in the Bible. His name in Hebrew is אַבְרָם (Avram).

people.name: Nahor
people.description: The brother of Abram, also the son of Terah. His name in Hebrew is נָחוֹר (Nachor), the same as his grandfather.

people.name: Haran
people.description: The brother of Abram and Nahor, and the father of Lot. His name in Hebrew is הָרָן (Haran).

people.name: Lot
people.description: The son of Haran, and the nephew of Abram. His name in Hebrew is לוֹט (Lot).

people.name: Sarai
people.description: The wife of Abram, later known as Sarah. Her name in Hebrew is שָׂרַי (Sarai).

people.name: Milcah
people.description: The daughter of Haran, and the wife of Nahor (Abram's brother). Her name in Hebrew is מִלְכָּה (Milkah).

people.name: Iscah
people.description: The daughter of Haran. Her name in Hebrew is יִסְכָּה (Yiskah).

place.name: Shinar
place.description: DescriptionShinar is the land where the people settled after the flood. It is often associated with the region of Mesopotamia, which is between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. In Genesis 11:2, it is described as the place where the people found a plain and decided to settle there.Hebrew RootThe Hebrew word for Shinar is שִׁנְעָר (Shin'ar), which is traditionally understood to refer to a region in southern Mesopotamia.

place.name: Babel
place.description: DescriptionBabel is the city where the Tower of Babel was constructed. It is significant for the account of the confusion of languages, which led to the scattering of people across the earth. Genesis 11:9 states, "Therefore it was called Babel, because there the LORD confused the language of the whole world."Hebrew RootThe name Babel (בָּבֶל, Bavel) is related to the Hebrew verb בָּלַל (balal), meaning "to confuse" or "to mix," reflecting the narrative of language confusion.

events.name: The Whole Earth Had One Language
events.description: The chapter begins by stating, "Now the whole world had one language and a common form of speech" (Genesis 11:1). The Hebrew word for "language" is "שָׂפָה" (safah), indicating a unified means of communication among all people.

events.name: The People Settle in Shinar
events.description: The people migrated from the east and settled in a plain in the land of Shinar (Genesis 11:2). "Shinar" is often associated with the region of Mesopotamia.

events.name: The Decision to Build a City and Tower
events.description: The people decided to build a city and a tower "with its top in the heavens" to make a name for themselves and prevent being scattered (Genesis 11:3-4). The Hebrew word for "tower" is "מִגְדָּל" (migdal), suggesting a large, fortified structure.

events.name: The LORD Comes Down to See the City and Tower
events.description: The text states, "Then the LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the sons of men were building" (Genesis 11:5). This anthropomorphic description emphasizes God's awareness and involvement.

events.name: The LORD Confuses Their Language
events.description: God observes that the people are unified and capable of achieving their plans, so He decides to "confuse their language" to prevent them from understanding one another (Genesis 11:6-7). The Hebrew root "בָּלַל" (balal) means to mix or confuse.

events.name: The Scattering of the People
events.description: As a result of the confusion of languages, the people are scattered "over the face of the whole earth" (Genesis 11:8-9). The city is named Babel, which sounds like the Hebrew word for "confused."

events.name: The Genealogy from Shem to Abram
events.description: The chapter transitions to a genealogy tracing the descendants of Shem down to Abram (Genesis 11:10-26). This genealogy serves as a bridge to the narrative of Abram (later Abraham), a key figure in biblical history.

events.name: The Introduction of Abram's Family
events.description: The chapter concludes with a brief introduction to Abram's family, including his father Terah and his brothers Nahor and Haran. It also mentions Sarai, Abram's wife, and Lot, his nephew (Genesis 11:27-32).
